items.title: Retrieval-Augmented LLM Agents: Learning to Learn from Experience
items.title_zh: 检索增强的 LLM 智能体：学会从经验中学习
items.summary: The authors combine LoRA fine-tuning with experience retrieval, integrating retrieved trajectories directly into the training process so agents learn to use them in context. They report substantially better generalization to unseen tasks, with gains that often persist with imperfect experience and even when agents reuse their own failed attempts without test-time parameter updates.

items.title: MemArchitect: A Policy Driven Memory Governance Layer
items.title_zh: MemArchitect：策略驱动的记忆治理层
items.summary: MemArchitect is a governance layer that separates memory lifecycle management from model weights and enforces rule-based policies for memory decay, conflict resolution and privacy. The authors report that governed memory outperforms unmanaged memory in agentic settings.

items.title: Retrieval-Augmented LLMs for Security Incident Analysis
items.title_zh: 面向安全事件分析的检索增强大语言模型
items.summary: The authors present a RAG-based system that uses a query library mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques to extract indicators from raw logs and retrieve context for forensic questions. Across eight LLM configurations, Claude Sonnet 4 reached 94% and DeepSeek V3 89% average recall on 17 malware scenarios, while locally deployed Llama 3.1:70b reached 81% at zero per-query cost.

items.title: Toward Evaluation Frameworks for Multi-Agent Scientific AI Systems
items.title_zh: 面向多智能体科研 AI 系统的评估框架探索
items.summary: This paper analyzes the challenges of benchmarking scientific multi-agent systems, including separating reasoning from retrieval, data and model contamination, missing ground truth for novel problems, tool use, and replication against a continuously changing knowledge base. It discusses strategies for contamination-resistant problems, scalable task families and multi-turn evaluation, and reports interviews with quantum-science researchers on how they expect to interact with AI systems.

items.title: FaithSteer-BENCH: A Deployment-Aligned Stress-Testing Benchmark for Inference-Time Steering
items.title_zh: FaithSteer-BENCH：面向部署的推理时引导压力测试基准
items.summary: FaithSteer-BENCH evaluates inference-time steering at a fixed deployment-style operating point, scoring controllability, utility preservation and robustness. The authors report illusory controllability, a cognitive tax on unrelated capabilities, and brittleness under mild perturbations.

items.title: Unified Policy Value Decomposition for Rapid Adaptation
items.title_zh: 面向快速适应的统一策略与价值分解
items.summary: The authors introduce a framework in which policy and value functions share a low-dimensional goal embedding that captures task identity, learned through a bilinear actor-critic decomposition built on Successor Features. With bases frozen at test time, a single forward pass estimates the goal coefficients and adapts a Soft Actor-Critic agent to novel locomotion directions without gradient updates.

items.title: Auditing Preferences for Brands and Cultures in LLMs
items.title_zh: 审计大语言模型对品牌与文化的偏好
items.summary: The paper introduces ChoiceEval, a reproducible framework that generates persona-diverse queries and converts free-form model outputs into comparable top-k choice sets to audit brand and cultural preferences. Applied to Gemini, GPT and DeepSeek across 10 topics and more than 2,000 questions, it finds US-developed models favor American entities while DeepSeek shows more balanced but still detectable geographic preferences.

items.title: Emergent Compositional Communication for Latent World Properties
items.title_zh: 面向潜在世界属性的涌现组合式通信
items.summary: Agents communicating through a Gumbel-Softmax bottleneck with iterated learning develop disentangled protocols for latent physical properties such as elasticity, friction and mass ratio without property labels; with four agents, all 80 seeds converged to near-perfect compositionality (PosDis=0.999, 98.3% holdout). The frozen protocol supports action-conditioned planning at 91.5% and transfers to real camera footage with 85.6% mass-comparison accuracy.
